page: Microsoft Azure F80amds_v7 is a high-density, compute and memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It provides 80 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per complex, alongside vector and cryptographic instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance is equipped with 640.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features an integrated 9,448 GB local NVMe SSD array for high-speed ephemeral data caching and scratch space. Accelerated hardware graphics are omitted, with zero GPUs present. Network integration does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network routing.

Benchmark measurements place the F80amds_v7 consistently in top-tier performance percentiles across compute and data-handling workloads. The instance registered 289,014.91 on stress-ng multi-core testing and 128,998.38 on PassMark CPU evaluations. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 467.51 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 209.76 GB/sec on uncached writes. Database and web serving tests yielded 196.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 109.14 GB/sec of static web throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F80amds_v7 concentrates dense execution capacity, vast memory bandwidth, and extensive onboard NVMe capacity onto a single host node, reducing cross-node network latency and node-management overhead. Given its heavy CPU density and memory allocation, it is best fitted for large in-memory databases, high-throughput caching nodes, real-time analytics engines, batch compression routines, and concurrent CPU-based inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F80amds_v7 is an enterprise-scale virtual instance driven by an 80-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz on dedicated single-threaded physical cores. Configured with 640.0 GB of RAM and 9,448 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, it delivers an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive and compute-bound tasks. The system features AVX-512 instruction set support, robust cryptographic accelerators, and top-tier memory bandwidth reaching 467.51 GB/sec on uncached read operations. Benchmark evaluations confirm top-tier throughput in multi-core compute, high-volume database operations, and Redis caching tests yielding over 196 million operations per second. Lacking integrated GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is engineered specifically for private network deployments, distributed in-memory data processing, large-scale Redis architectures, enterprise web serving, and heavy CPU-based model inference.
